answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to lock a refundable stake that unlocks only after months of honest work. Like water hidden in karst, the deposit sits out of sight, but peers who prove fraud can drain it through slashing. An attacker spawning ten thousand fake agents must freeze an ocean of capital and lose it when the puppets are exposed, so faking a crowd costs far more than earning trust slowly, the way yarrow takes seasons to root in thin soil.
